unit.title: Your first financial plan
unit.description: Saving, investing or speculating, goals with a date, how much risk you can handle and what the trading data says

texts: The trendy coin
Nico
Put €5,000 into this coin! It's gone up 300 % this month and everyone's piling in
You've got €12,000 saved and you spend €1,200 a month.
What do you do?
I put in the €5,000: I don't want to miss out
That's **FOMO**, the fear of missing out. Buying because it's already shot up is speculating… with almost half your savings.
At most, a small amount I could afford to lose completely
Good: you only speculate **with what you can afford to lose**. Before that, your cushion and long-term investing.
I give him my passwords so he can manage it for me
Never give anyone control of your money or your passwords! It's the way in for loads of scams.
Save for what's near, invest for what's far off and only speculate with what you can afford to lose.
Save, invest or speculate?

• **Saving:** setting money aside without risking it, for things that are close.
• **Investing:** putting money into things that **produce value** (companies, loans, property), for 5 years or more.
• **Speculating:** buying in the hope that someone else will buy it from you for more soon.
Saving
Investing
Speculating
Interest-paying account for the summer trip
You need it soon and with no risk: saving.
Paying into a global index fund every month for 20 years
You buy a tiny slice of thousands of profit-making companies: investing.
A new coin because people on TikTok say it's «going to the moon»
It produces nothing: you're just hoping someone else pays more. Speculating.
Treasury bills for a deposit on a flat, a year from now
Short term and no risk of falls: saving.
Leveraged CFDs to make money in a week
Short-term, multiplied bets: pure speculation.
Shares in lots of companies for 15 years from now
Company profits, diversified and long term: investing.
Sort the six cases.

Ask yourself **where the gain comes from**: interest (saving), what the thing you buy produces (investing) or the pocket of someone else who gets it right less often than you (speculating). Try it: in Market, compare the bitcoin chart with a global ETF's.
Hint: does it produce anything, or are you just hoping it goes up?
Sort each case

u4l2.title: Goals with a date and an amount

texts: «I want to save more»
Sara
This year I'm going to… save more!
What's this goal missing?
Nothing, it's a perfect goal
«Save more» can't be measured: how much? By when? What for? That way there's no telling whether you've hit it.
An amount, a date and a reason
That's it! A good goal is **SMART**: specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound.
More motivation
Motivation helps, but without an amount or a date you don't know if you're on track. A concrete goal is more motivating.
OK: I want **€900** to go travelling in the summer, 6 months from now.
Much better! That's €150 a month. And what if you have several goals at once?
Your goals, in numbers
Sara has three goals and can put aside **€250 a month**. For each one: what she needs ÷ the months left = what she has to put aside.
Summer trip
New laptop
Driving licence
With €250 a month, can Sara reach all three goals in those timeframes?
Yes, with some to spare
No: she'd need €400 a month
She's only a few euros short
Change the timeframes so everything fits into €250 a month.
If you can't make it, don't give up: **move the date** or the amount. And keep each goal in its own «savings pot», so you don't spend the trip money on the laptop.
That doesn't add up: she's more than €100 a month short.
Almost! A bit more time on one of them and it fits.
Stretch the timeframe of whatever's least urgent

steps.title: Each goal in its place
steps.body:
You already know that **the time frame decides the risk** you can take. Apply it to each goal:

• **Under 3 years** (trip, driving licence, laptop): saved in an interest-bearing account, deposits or Treasury bills.
• **15 years or more** (retirement, financial freedom): mostly diversified shares, with regular contributions.
• **In between:** a prudent mix, with more bonds the closer it gets.
steps.key: The date of each goal decides whether you save for it or invest for it.
steps.tip: Try it: buy a global ETF in the simulator for your most distant goal.

u4l4.title: How much risk you can handle

texts: Live through the 2008 crisis
It's October 2007. You invest **€10,000** in the S&P 500. Hit «Start» and watch how it moves week by week, with **real data**. You can sell whenever you like.
Make it to the end, whether you sell or not.

This is **risk tolerance**: how far you can watch your money fall without panic selling. The fall reached 56 %. Those who sold at the bottom turned a temporary fall into a real loss; those who held on got their money back in 2013 (not counting dividends).
You've sold. Now watch what happens next…
Your investment has lost almost half its value. The news says this is only just getting started. Will you hold on?
Down 20 %… how are you feeling?
You're already up! This is easy… isn't it?
Hit «Start». You can sell whenever you like

steps.title: Capacity and tolerance
steps.body:
**Risk capacity:** how much you can lose **without it changing your life** (income, cushion, dependants, time horizon). It's objective.

**Risk tolerance:** how far you can watch your money fall **without panic selling**. It's psychological, and almost everyone overestimates it when the market is rising.

Your real profile is **the lower of the two**. When you open an account with a European broker, they'll give you a **MiFID test**: answer it honestly, it protects you from products you don't understand.
steps.key: Everyone's brave when the market is going up.
steps.tip: Try it: in Market, open the S&P 500 with monthly candles and find its worst fall.

u4l5.title: The truth about getting rich quick

texts: The Instagram guru
@MillionaireAt22
A year ago I was a waiter. Now I make **€5,000 a month** trading from the beach
Copy my trades for just **€99 a month**. Only 10 spots left! Open an account with this broker using my link
How many red flags can you spot?
None: if he earns that much, he must know what he's doing
If he really made €5,000 a month trading, why would he need to sell you anything? He makes money from **your** subscription and the broker's commission.
Several: the promises, the rush, the subscription and the broker link
All of them! He promises a lot without showing his full track record, rushes you («10 spots»), sells subscriptions and gets paid for bringing you to a broker.
Just one: that he charges €99
There are more: the rush, the promises with no track record and the link to a specific broker, which he usually gets paid for.
Before paying anyone, look them up with the **CNMV** and on its list of unauthorised firms.
Try it: in the simulator, do the boring thing: put money into a global ETF every month.
«5 % every week»
Ana
Someone's sent me a platform that pays **5 % every week**. Guaranteed!
At that rate, what would €1,000 turn into in three years?
About €9,000
That would be just adding. Compounding every week, it's more than **€2 million**.
More than €2 million
That's it: €1,000 × 1.05 every week, for 156 weeks. Nobody who could do that would need your money.
I don't know, but it sounds good
Always do the sum: at that rate, €1,000 would be more than €2 million in three years.
Put like that… so where does the money that pays the first ones come from?
Often, from those who join later. When they stop coming in, it's over.

steps.title: Before you pay anyone
steps.body:
• **Are they authorised?** Look them up in the CNMV register and on its list of warnings about unauthorised firms («chiringuitos financieros»).
• **Do they show their whole track record?** A few screenshots of good days aren't one.
• **What do they live on?** If they charge for courses, signals or for sending you to a broker, they win even if you lose.
• **Do they promise?** High and safe returns don't exist.
steps.key: Someone who really knows how to make money investing doesn't need to sell you the method.

s1boss.title: Final challenge: Your money in order

u4l1-1.prompt: Match each activity with where its gain comes from.
u4l1-1.explanation: The key question is always the same: where does the gain come from?
right: Profits, interest or rent over the long term
Interest without risking what you put in

u4l1-3.prompt: You need the money for a trip in a year's time. What makes most sense?
options: Saving it in an account or deposit
u4l1-3.explanation: With a one-year horizon, the money shouldn't be in something that can drop 30 %.

u4l1-4.prompt: Where does the gain come from for someone who invests in a company for the long term?
options: From the profits the company makes
u4l1-4.explanation: Investing means sharing in what the asset produces: profits, interest or rent.

u4l1-7.prompt: Buying a crypto because «everyone says it's going to go up» is investing.
u4l1-7.explanation: It's speculating: the gain depends on someone else paying more, not on what the asset produces.

u4l1-9.prompt: Save for what's near, invest for what's ____ and only speculate with what you can afford to lose.
u4l1-9.explanation: The further away the goal, the more time there is to recover from falls.

u4l1-10.prompt: Which are examples of speculating? Tick all.
options: Buying a trendy coin because it's going up
Paying into a global fund every month for 20 years
u4l1-10.explanation: Paying into a diversified fund for the long term is investing.

u4l2-1.prompt: Put the steps for working out your monthly contribution in order.
options: Divide what's missing by the months left
u4l2-1.explanation: Amount, date, starting point and division: that's how a wish becomes a monthly plan.

u4l2-4.prompt: A SMART goal is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and has a ____.
u4l2-4.explanation: Without a deadline you can't work out how much to put in each month.

options: Having €12,000 for a car in 2029 by putting in €250 a month
u4l2-5.explanation: It has an amount, a date and a plan: it can be measured and tracked.

u4l2-6.prompt: Is it just a wish or a measurable goal?
options: €4,000 for a master's in September 2027, with €250 a month
u4l2-6.explanation: An amount and a date turn a wish into something you can track month by month.

u4l2-9.prompt: Ana wants a €3,000 cushion, a €1,500 trip in the summer and a deposit on a flat in 6 years. She keeps it all together in the same account. What should she do?
options: Keep it all together: it's simpler
Put each goal in its own account or savings pot
Go for one goal at a time and forget the rest
u4l2-9.explanation: One pot per goal: that way the money for each target doesn't get mixed up.
feedback: In the summer she won't know how much she can spend without touching the cushion or the flat money.
She can see how far along she is with each, and the trip doesn't eat into the cushion.
Meanwhile, the clock keeps ticking on the other goals.

u4l2-11.prompt: Save or invest for this goal?
u4l2-11.explanation: What you need in under 3 years can't depend on the stock market not falling that day; distant goals have time to recover from falls. Investing it all «so it grows more» is tempting, but the time frame rules.

u4l2-12.prompt: Sara wants €1,200 for a laptop in 8 months. A friend tells her to put it in shares «so it grows more». What does she do?
options: She saves it in an interest-bearing account
She puts it all in shares
She puts it in a trendy crypto
u4l2-12.explanation: Over 8 months, the money has to be available and safe from falls. Shares are tempting because they usually grow more, but only over the long run and with falls along the way.
feedback: In 8 months she'll have all her money, whatever happens in the market.
If the market falls 20 % just before, she's left without a laptop or has to wait.
Even more risk for money she needs soon and by a set date.

options: The lower of capacity and tolerance
The higher of capacity and tolerance
u4l4-1.explanation: If you can lose a lot but can't stomach it, you'll panic sell; if you can stomach it but can't afford it, you're taking too much risk.

u4l4-2.prompt: Match each concept with its meaning.
u4l4-2.explanation: Capacity and horizon are objective; tolerance is psychological.
right: How far you can watch it fall without selling
How much you can lose without it changing your life

u4l4-3.prompt: Marta is 23, has a stable job, a 6-month cushion and invests for 30 years from now in a diversified portfolio. Her portfolio drops 35 %. Which decision fits her plan?
options: Sells everything so as not to lose more
Sticks to the plan and keeps up her contributions
Takes out a loan to buy more
u4l4-3.explanation: With capacity and time on her side, the plan matters more than the day's headline.
feedback: She turns a temporary fall into a permanent loss and, if there's a rebound later, she misses it.
Her time horizon and her cushion let her wait: the fall is only a real loss if she sells.
Borrowing to invest multiplies the risk: if it keeps falling, she owes money and loses.

u4l4-7.prompt: Does this add to or take away from your risk capacity?
u4l4-7.explanation: Capacity depends on your objective situation: income, cushion, dependants and time horizon.

u4l4-10.prompt: You get very nervous when you see red numbers and you'll need the money in 3 years. Your profile is…
u4l4-10.explanation: Low tolerance and a short horizon: lots of bonds and few shares.

u4l4-11.prompt: Your portfolio falls 50 %. To get back to where it was, how much does it then have to rise?
u4l4-11.explanation: After falling by half, recovering means doubling what's left: 100 %. It's tempting to think 50 % is enough, but that 50 % is worked out on a much smaller amount. That's why big falls are so hard to recover from.

u4l5-3.prompt: Tick the messages that look like a scam or a guru.
options: Remember: CFDs are complex and most retail accounts lose money on them.
I've started putting €50 a month into an index fund. Boring, but here goes
We guarantee 5 % a week with no risk. Open an account with this broker using my link.
I quit my job thanks to trading. My VIP course, today only, €497
100 % accurate buy signals. Limited places: join before midnight.
u4l5-3.explanation: Promises of guaranteed gains, pressure to hurry and links to a specific broker are classic signs.

u4l5-6.prompt: What are signs of a scam? Tick all.
options: Registered with the CNMV, with a risk document
u4l5-6.explanation: A legitimate firm is registered and explains its risks and costs.

u4l5-7.prompt: An influencer with a luxury car offers to let you copy his trades for €99 a month: «last month I made 40 %». What do you do?
options: I also give him my broker login so he can trade for me
I sign up: the results speak for themselves
I check whether he's registered with the CNMV and ask for his full track record
u4l5-7.explanation: Before paying anyone: CNMV registration, full track record and no rushing.
feedback: Never share your login details: he could empty your account.
A screenshot of one good month says nothing about the bad months he doesn't show.
He isn't registered and only has screenshots of good days: you save €99 a month and probably a lot more.

u4l5-10.prompt: What works: investing regularly, diversifying, low costs, lots of time and no ____ selling.
u4l5-10.explanation: Panic selling turns temporary falls into real losses.

u4l5-11.prompt: Match each guru line with the trick behind it.
right: Earns a commission from the broker
Rushes you so you don't think it over
u4l5-11.explanation: Hurry, screenshots, affiliate links and guarantees: four tricks that keep coming back.

u4l5-12.prompt: An «adviser» calls you. His firm isn't in the CNMV register, but it has a very professional website and customer reviews. What do you do?
options: I try with a small amount
I trust him: the website looks very serious
I give him no money: without authorisation there's nothing more to look at
feedback: You can lose a small amount too, and then they'll ask for more to «win it back».
A website and some reviews can be made up in an afternoon. An authorisation can't.
That's it. If the firm isn't authorised, it can't provide you with investment services, however good it sounds.
u4l5-12.explanation: The first thing is to check the authorisation with the CNMV. Without it, go no further.
